gaps.concept: Ectocervix has nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium; endocervix has mucus-secreting simple columnar epithelium.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the tissue and cell type shown on cervical histology. [Source](https://extranet.who.int/ncdccs/Data/ZMB_D1_VIA-CryoReferenceManualZambiaMarch2015.pdf)

gaps.concept: Estrogen makes cervical mucus thin and permeable to sperm; progesterone makes it thick and relatively impermeable.
gaps.why_tested: Explains mucus changes across the menstrual cycle or with hormonal contraception.

gaps.concept: HPV 6 and 11 are low-risk types associated with condylomata, unlike oncogenic HPV 16 and 18.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a wart-associated HPV type from one associated with cervical cancer. [Source](https://www.cdc.gov/pinkbook/hcp/table-of-contents/chapter-11-human-papillomavirus.html)

gaps.concept: Persistent high-risk HPV infection over years, rather than transient infection, drives progression to cervical precancer and cancer.
gaps.why_tested: Explains why most HPV infections resolve while a persistent infection can progress. [Source](https://www.cancer.gov/types/cervical/causes-risk-prevention)

gaps.concept: Integration of high-risk HPV DNA can disrupt viral E2, increasing E6 and E7 expression.
gaps.why_tested: Connects viral integration in a tumor specimen to increased oncogene expression. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3945621/)

gaps.concept: HPV E7-mediated Rb inactivation increases p16 expression; diffuse p16 staining supports an HPV-associated high-grade lesion.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets p16 immunostaining on a cervical biopsy. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3945621/)

gaps.concept: CIN 1, 2, and 3 involve atypia in the lower third, lower two thirds, and nearly full epithelial thickness, respectively.
gaps.why_tested: Assigns a CIN grade from the depth of epithelial atypia on biopsy. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK321760/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK321760.pdf)

gaps.concept: CIN remains above an intact basement membrane; stromal invasion distinguishes invasive cervical carcinoma.
gaps.why_tested: Separates carcinoma in situ from invasive cancer on histology. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK424408/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK424408.pdf)

gaps.concept: HPV 18 is particularly associated with cervical glandular neoplasia, including adenocarcinoma arising in the endocervix.
gaps.why_tested: Links a gland-forming endocervical lesion to its characteristic HPV association. [Source](https://dceg.cancer.gov/news-events/news/2020/hpv-genotyping)

gaps.concept: Cervical cancer can present with postcoital bleeding or persistent watery, blood-tinged vaginal discharge.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes the symptomatic cervical cancer vignette. [Source](https://www.cancer.gov/types/cervical/symptoms)

gaps.concept: In utero diethylstilbestrol exposure increases the risk of cervical clear cell adenocarcinoma.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cervical cancer associated with maternal DES use. [Source](https://www.cancer.gov/types/cervical/causes-risk-prevention)

gaps.concept: Cervical dysplasia often appears acetowhite after acetic acid application during colposcopy.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies an abnormal area targeted for cervical biopsy. [Source](https://publications.iarc.who.int/_publications/media/download/4577/f2c8072ead1ed906e8bdb439fd36ffdd707bba2a.pdf)

gaps.concept: HPV vaccination prevents new infections but does not treat existing infection; vaccinated patients still need cervical screening.
gaps.why_tested: Tests prevention counseling after vaccination or a positive HPV result. [Source](https://www.cdc.gov/cervical-cancer/prevention/index.html)

gaps.concept: Prior CIN 2 or worse requires prolonged surveillance after treatment, including beyond age 65 when applicable.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes routine screening cessation from follow-up after high-grade precancer. [Source](https://asccp.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/2019_ASCCP_Risk_Based_Management_Consensus.3.pdf)

gaps.concept: LEEP or cone excision increases the risk of subsequent preterm birth through cervical weakening.
gaps.why_tested: Explains an obstetric complication after treatment of cervical dysplasia. [Source](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/loop-electrosurgical-excision-procedure)

gaps.concept: HPV 16 or 18 positivity warrants colposcopic evaluation even when concurrent cervical cytology is negative.
gaps.why_tested: Tests risk-based follow-up for a discordant HPV-positive, Pap-negative result. [Source](https://asccp.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/2019_ASCCP_Risk_Based_Management_Consensus.3.pdf)
